name: settings-action-rows
note: UAT batch 5 ('too cluttered w text. simplicity FTW. UI standard layout? for export etc buttons, min prose'). RED-FIRST vs main: six rows doing the same job wore FOUR different looks - a bordered .setRow card with a stacked description, an .aboutLink with an icon and a wrapping sentence, a .btn.ghost pair, and a raw URL as body text - because there was no convention to conform to. Now every 'do a thing' row is .setAction: one line, verb-first, no prose. The uniformity assert compares each row against the FIRST one measured rather than pinning a height, so a future restyle of the primitive cannot pass this while the rows diverge again.

steps.label: layout settle gate: await document.fonts.ready before any geometry assert
every action in the section is the SAME primitive - no lookalike row survives beside it
the rows are uniform - each matches the FIRST row's height and box, compared measured-to-measured so a restyle of the primitive cannot pass this while they diverge
min prose: every row is ONE line and none of them clips - a label that needed the ellipsis guard would mean the label is too long, not that the row should wrap
no row carries a description - the row IS the label
the section opens with ONE caption, not a wall (it was two full paragraphs plus a three-line raw URL)
a row that LEAVES the app is distinguishable without a sentence saying so - external ink plus the leave-app glyph
Backup rows take the same primitive, and .saMeta carries live STATE only - value alone, never repeating the row's own label back at it
no horizontal overflow at 412 with the new rows
